jobs.title: Director - Enterprise Data Modernization Lead (GCP)
jobs.description:
Position Description

We are seeking a Director, Consulting Expert (DCE) – Enterprise Data Warehouse & Data Platforms to provide senior technical, solutioning, and client facing leadership

The DCE will serve as a trusted advisor to the client while helping shape, win, govern, and successfully deliver complex enterprise data initiatives.

This is not a narrow technical specialist or delivery only position. The DCE combines deep enterprise data warehouse and modern data platform expertise with consulting acumen, architecture leadership, commercial awareness, and executive presence. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable discussing business outcomes with senior client stakeholders, shaping and estimating solutions, leading architecture decisions, and engaging in detailed technical discussions with engineering teams.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Serve as a senior client facing advisor for enterprise data warehouse, data engineering, analytics, and data platform modernization initiatives within a complex telecommunications environment.
Translate business objectives and requirements into actionable data strategies, architectures, roadmaps, and solution options.
Lead end to end solution architecture, considering data, applications, integration, cloud, cybersecurity, operations, cost, scalability, and delivery trade offs.
Architect and guide enterprise data solutions on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including technologies such as BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Dataflow, Dataproc, Pub/Sub, Cloud Composer, Dataplex, Dataform, and Looker.
Provide technical leadership across enterprise data warehousing, data modelling, ETL/ELT, batch and streaming pipelines, data quality, metadata, governance, security, and analytics.
Lead or co lead technical solutioning for strategic pursuits, proposals, RFPs, and account growth opportunities.
Develop and challenge solution scope, architecture, assumptions, estimates, resource models, dependencies, risks, and delivery approaches to ensure solutions are competitive and executable.
Orchestrate SMEs across data, cloud, applications, integration, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and operations to develop cohesive end to end solutions.
Lead or participate in architecture, estimation, proposal, and delivery governance reviews, identifying technical and delivery risks before commitments are made.
Advise on AI/ML and generative AI data readiness, including data quality, accessibility, governance, privacy, security, and responsible adoption.
Maintain sufficient hands on technical depth to challenge designs, validate assumptions, troubleshoot critical issues, and defend architectural decisions.
Mentor architects and technical leads and promote reusable architectures, patterns, accelerators, and solution assets across the team.
Partner with the DCS and broader P&L leadership to strengthen the client relationship, identify growth opportunities, improve solution quality, and develop technical leadership capability within the team.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

10+ years of progressively responsible experience in leading enterprise data warehousing, data engineering, analytics, cloud architecture, solution architecture, or related IT consulting disciplines.
Demonstrated experience architecting and delivering complex enterprise data warehouse and modern cloud data platform solutions.
Strong experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and its data and analytics ecosystem, particularly Big Query and associated ingestion, processing, orchestration, governance, and analytics capabilities.
Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, data modelling, ETL/ELT, data integration, data quality, metadata, security, governance, and analytics.
Strong SQL skills and working knowledge of modern data engineering technologies and practices such as Python, Git, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, APIs, and automated testing/deployment.
Experience with enterprise data technologies such as Snowflake, Databricks, Oracle, SQL Server, Teradata, Informatica, DataStage, dbt, or comparable platforms.
Demonstrated experience leading solution architecture for significant client engagements, proposals, RFPs, or complex technology pursuits.
Experience developing or validating solution estimates, delivery models, assumptions, dependencies, and technical risks.
Strong consulting and executive communication skills, including discovery, problem framing, facilitation, solution development, and client presentations.
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary technical teams, influence senior stakeholders, and mentor architects and technical leaders.
Working knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI concepts and their implications for enterprise data architecture and governance.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience delivering data and analytics solutions within the telecommunications industry, with an understanding of large scale, high volume telco data environments and associated business and operational use cases.
Google Cloud certification, particularly Professional Cloud Architect and/or Professional Data Engineer, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
Experience modernizing large legacy or on premises enterprise data warehouse environments to GCP.
Experience within a large IT consulting, systems integration, managed services, or professional services organization.
Experience supporting large, complex and highly integrated enterprise technology environments.
Commercial awareness encompassing consulting economics, solution costing, delivery risk, and value based solutioning.

Leadership Profile

The successful DCE will be a visible, take charge consulting leader who:

Leads with client and business outcomes rather than technology alone.
Has the executive presence to independently lead senior client conversations.
Takes ownership of ambiguous or difficult solution problems and drives them to resolution.
Retains enough hands on technical depth to challenge and defend important architecture decisions.
Challenges unrealistic estimates, unsupported assumptions, scope gaps, and delivery risks before commitments are made.
Works across organizational and technology boundaries rather than operating as a narrow or isolated SME.
Coaches and develops architects and technical leaders, raising the capability of the broader team.

Measures of Success

Success will be reflected in stronger client relationships, higher quality solutions and estimates, improved pursuit outcomes, reduced delivery risk, successful enterprise data initiatives, and increased technical capability across the team.

The DCE will be recognized by the client, delivery teams, DCS, and broader P&L leadership as a trusted senior advisor who connects telecommunications business outcomes, enterprise data architecture, technology, commercial realities, and delivery feasibility.

CGI is providing a reasonable estimate of the pay range for this role. The determination of this range includes factors such as skill set level, geographic market, experience and training, and licenses and certifications. Compensation decisions depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $115,000–$165,000. This role is an existing vacancy.

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

jobs.title: Director Enterprise Resources Planning
jobs.description:
Ready to shape the future of ERP technology in a multibillion dollar global business?

Want the freedom to challenge the status quo, lead major transformation & make a lasting impact across international operations?

Our client is a major publicly listed aviation business with operations across North America and Europe. Combining the scale and resources of a global organisation with the pace, autonomy and entrepreneurial spirit of a much smaller company, the business is investing in technology, innovation and operational excellence to support its continued growth.

We’re seeking a Director, ERP
to take global ownership of the Quantum Control ERP platform, lead an international team and drive improvements in systems, data integrity and operational processes. This newly created Director, ERP position offers significant strategic influence, including the opportunity to shape the technology roadmap and potentially lead the early stages of a major ERP replacement.

What’s in it for you

C$210k–C$260k base salary plus 10% to 15% discretionary annual bonus, healthcare & 401(k) contributions
A newly created Director, ERP role with genuine autonomy, global responsibility & direct access to senior leadership
Opportunity to shape the ERP strategy, introduce new technologies & influence a potential global system replacement
Join a growing, entrepreneurial business where decisions are made quickly, innovation is encouraged & your contribution will have a lasting impact
Lead & develop an international team of 6 to 8 ERP professionals, with potential for further growth

You’ll be responsible for

Owning the global Quantum Control ERP platform, defining its strategy, roadmap, priorities & ongoing improvement
Leading, coaching & developing a geographically distributed ERP team across multiple international locations
Improving data integrity, standardising processes & ensuring consistency across manufacturing and repair facilities
Driving ERP integrations with production planning, maintenance, quality, finance & other operational systems
Partnering with senior leadership to prioritise improvements, deliver business value & potentially lead the early stages of a future ERP replacement

You’ll need

7+ years of enterprise ERP experience, including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, NetSuite or Quantum Control
3+ years of people management experience, ideally leading teams across multiple locations
Strong experience in complex manufacturing or supply chain environments, with aviation or MRO experience beneficial but not essential
Proven ability to lead ERP improvements, integrations, process standardisation & technology transformation, with strong understanding of ERP data structures and workflows
A proactive, commercially minded leadership style, with the confidence to challenge existing processes, make decisions & take ownership of results

Location

New York or Montreal preferred, with Miami also considered. Primarily onsite, typically 5 days per week, with international travel to operational facilities. Initial travel may be required every 2 to 3 weeks, reducing as relationships and processes become established.

All candidates will be considered without regard to race, gender, age, national origin, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law. Every application will be reviewed by a real person and responded to.

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO)
is an agency where innovation thrives, ideas flourish, and passion drives us to new heights of excellence. Reporting to the Ministry of the Attorney General, the AGCO is responsible for regulating Ontario’s vibrant alcohol, gaming, horse racing, and private retail cannabis sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is seeking a strategic, collaborative and forward-thinking leader to serve as Director, People and Culture Strategy. Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), the Director People and Culture Strategy provides enterprise leadership for People and Culture strategy, transformation and modernization, with responsibility for advancing the People Strategic Plan, divisional priorities, enterprise metrics and executive reporting, HR digital enablement, responsible AI adoption, diversity, inclusion and accessibility (DI&A), inclusive leadership and high-performing team leadership.

This role translates enterprise and divisional priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, implementation plans, performance measures and governance mechanisms that strengthen organizational readiness, workforce planning, evidence-based decision-making and measurable impact across AGCO.

The ideal candidate is a trusted strategic advisor who brings strong judgment, systems thinking and a collaborative leadership style. They are comfortable operating in a complex public-sector environment, balancing long-term transformation with immediate operational priorities, and translating data, risk, workforce trends and stakeholder needs into practical, inclusive and measurable people strategies.

If you are motivated by the opportunity to lead strategic HR transformation, advance responsible digital and AI adoption, strengthen diversity, inclusion and accessibility, and support a strong employee experience, this role offers a meaningful platform to make a lasting enterprise-wide contribution at AGCO.

What You Will Do

Lead the development, implementation and ongoing refresh of AGCO’s People Strategic Plan, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities, government mandates, workforce risks and evolving organizational needs.
Translate organizational priorities into actionable people strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, performance measures and implementation plans.
Oversee the planning, prioritization and delivery of People and Culture initiatives, projects and divisional priorities that advance organizational goals.
Establish planning, governance, reporting and accountability mechanisms to monitor progress against strategic commitments and demonstrate measurable impact.
Provide strategic advice to the CHRO, C-Suite, senior leaders and governance committees on HR priorities, workforce implications, transformation risks and organizational readiness.
Design and oversee enterprise People and Culture performance indicators, dashboards, workforce analytics and executive reporting to support transparency, accountability and evidence-informed decision-making.
Lead HR digital enablement and responsible AI adoption by developing practical capability, governance practices and high-value use cases that improve service quality, efficiency and decision-making.
Provide enterprise leadership for DI&A strategy, accessibility and inclusive leadership, embedding inclusion principles into AGCO culture, operations and people practices.
Lead the refresh, implementation and evaluation of enterprise DI&A strategy, including the development and reporting of meaningful performance measures.
Act as a senior subject matter expert on DI&A and accessibility, advising executives and senior leaders on inclusive talent practices, cultural transformation and emerging obligations.
Provide leadership and direction to a team by setting clear expectations, prioritizing deliverables, supporting development and fostering a culture of inclusion, accountability, learning and high

You Have

Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Organizational Psychology, Adult Education, Strategic Planning, Leadership, Human Rights, Public Policy or a related field, or equivalent work experience; a master’s degree is considered an asset.
Minimum of 8 years progressive leadership experience in strategic planning, organizational transformation, HR strategy, performance measurement, workforce analytics, DI&A, accessibility, digital enablement and/or related areas.
Demonstrated ability to translate enterprise priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, governance structures, implementation plans and measurable outcomes.
Strong understanding of HR digital adoption, HRIS-enabled process improvement, workflow automation, workforce analytics, digital service delivery, change management and responsible AI use.
Knowledge of HR data governance, privacy, accessibility, security, records management and ethical use of workforce information.
Experience developing executive-level reports, dashboards, briefings and presentations that translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.
Strong consultation, facilitation, public speaking and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence and build alignment across senior leaders, governance bodies and cross-functional partners.
Demonstrated experience leading DI&A strategy, accessibility initiatives, inclusive leadership development, employee engagement forums, committees or enterprise-wide measurement frameworks.
Strong knowledge of Ontario legal and regulatory frameworks related to human rights, accessibility, employment standards and inclusive workplace practices.
Experience leading, coaching and developing teams in a complex, unionized and public-sector environment is an asset.
Eligibility to work in Canada and the ability to successfully complete a criminal background check.

To apply to this vacancy, please submit your application online at our Careers webpage located at Careers | Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario. Please note that only applications submitted through the Applicant Tracking System will be accepted.

About The AGCO

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is an Ontario provincial regulatory agency that reports to the Ministry of the Attorney General. We are responsible for regulating the alcohol, gaming, horse racing and cannabis retail sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The AGCO is proud to be recognized as one of Greater Toronto’s Top Employers for the second year in a row. This annual distinction reflects our commitment to cultivating a workplace environment that prioritizes employee well-being, emphasizing work-life balance, mental health resources, and opportunities for professional growth. We remain committed to fostering a supportive and rewarding work environment for our employees.

Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

As the Senior Director, Strategy Risk Business Operations and Shared Services you will lead a high-performing team of directors, senior managers, and managers to drive strategic, operational, and financial excellence within RBC’s Commercial & Payment Technology (CPT) portfolio. This critical leadership role is accountable for Financial Management, Project Portfolio Planning, Vendor Management, Risk & Compliance, and Strategic Planning, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities and delivering exceptional business outcomes. You will champion employee engagement, change management, and innovation (e.g., AI adoption) while maintaining rigorous governance and operational excellence.

What You'll Do

Leadership & Strategy

Lead the Planning, Risk & Governance functions, overseeing financial management, project portfolio planning, and strategic alignment with RBC’s Commercial Banking and T&O objectives.
Develop and execute CPT’s 5-year strategic plan, leveraging internal/external research and partnering with business executives to drive disciplined project management.
Champion enterprise initiatives (e.g., AI/AIDLC) and change management within CPT, ensuring successful adoption and engagement.
Foster exceptional employee engagement through targeted strategies and communication plans in partnership with Enterprise Communications.

Risk & Governance

Ensure adherence to Risk & Governance policies, standards, and control points (e.g., audits, access reviews, compliance attestations).
Lead T&O and RBC-initiated Risk & Governance campaigns, collaborating with Risk, GS, and business partners.
Oversee Business Continuity Management (BCM), including plan approvals, testing, and strategy.
Monitor Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and escalate issues, ensuring alignment with first-line defense (Internal/External Audit).

Vendor Management

Lead the expansion of Vendor Management, optimizing on-shore/off-shore resources and negotiating multi-million-dollar contracts.
Drive cost savings, efficiencies, and service standards across vendor relationships, ensuring alignment with financial and operational targets.

Financial Management & Reporting

Define and execute the Financial Plan for application maintenance, development, and Risk & Governance efforts.
Provide timely, actionable financial reporting (budgets, forecasts, metrics) to the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) and stakeholders.
Manage IT Development, Maintenance, and Financial budgets, ensuring alignment with annual and 5-year plans.
Oversee project accruals, cost accounting, and vendor invoice management to meet overhead and recovery targets.

Operational Excellence & Performance

Monitor performance metrics, scorecards, and dashboards, driving process improvements and benchmarking.
Lead Program/Project onboarding/closure, ensuring accurate financial tracking in systems (e.g., Planview, MIS).
Leverage AI and automation for reporting and project delivery efficiencies.

People Leadership

Build and mentor a high-performing team, aligning individual goals with RBC’s Leadership Model.
Drive diversity, reward & recognition, and career development initiatives.
Instill a culture of change readiness and empowerment across CPT.

What You Need To Succeed

Must Have:

15+ years of leadership experience in Technology, Financial Services, or Operations, with expertise in Risk, Governance, and Vendor Management.
Proven track record in strategic planning, financial management, and large-scale project delivery.
Strong understanding of AI, Agile/SDLC methodologies, and regulatory compliance.
Exceptional negotiation, stakeholder management, and communication skills.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or related field; MBA or advanced certification preferred.

Nice to Have:

Payments industry experience

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
About Allied

Allied is a leading owner-operator of distinctive urban workspace in Canada’s major cities. Our work is grounded in a clear purpose: to provide knowledge-based organizations with distinctive urban environments that support creativity, connectivity and human wellness.

Our vision is more expansive. We seek to make a continuous contribution to cities and culture that elevates and inspires the humanity in all of us. This vision informs how we operate, how we design and how we lead.

Real estate, for us, is not a passive investment. It is a profoundly human endeavour, one that must promote wellness, sustainability, diversity and creativity—today and for generations to come.

Allied is also a place to build a career of consequence. If you are looking for work that is thoughtful, tangible and enduring—work that contributes meaningfully to cities and the people who inhabit them—you will find purpose here.

For more information on Allied’s approach to city-building, visit our Insights page.

Purpose

Lead Allied’s financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis and management reporting activities.
As Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), you will lead budgeting and forecasting processes, develop long-term financial plans and provide analysis of financial and operating performance across Allied’s portfolio and corporate functions.

As a key member of the Finance leadership team, you will serve as a strategic business partner to senior leaders and help strengthen financial planning, analytical capabilities and financial discipline across the organization. This role is well suited to a collaborative and forward-looking finance leader with strong financial modelling and analytical capabilities and a commitment to developing people and building high-performing teams.

Responsibilities

Financial Planning, Budgeting and Forecasting
Lead budgeting and forecasting processes across the organization, establishing timelines, assumptions and requirements in partnership with key stakeholders.
Develop and own consolidated financial forecasts and multi-year financial plans.
Establish and track key performance indicators related to occupancy, leasing, operating performance, capital expenditures, financing and other business drivers.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to assess the financial implications of changing business and market conditions.
Continuously enhance planning and forecasting processes to improve accuracy, efficiency and business insight.

Performance Analysis and Management Reporting
Lead the preparation of monthly and quarterly management reporting for senior leadership.
Analyze actual financial performance relative to budget, forecast and prior periods, identifying key drivers of variances.
Analyze key performance indicators, including funds from operations (FFO), adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) and related financial and operating metrics.
Identify emerging trends, risks and opportunities and communicate their potential financial impact to senior leadership.
Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards and other reporting tools that provide clear visibility into organizational performance.
Lead the development of financial and performance reporting for the Board of Trustees and its committees.

Long-Term Financial Planning and Strategic Analysis
Lead the development and maintenance of Allied’s long-term financial model.
Assess the impact of changes in occupancy, leasing activity, rental rates, interest rates, capital expenditures, development activity and other key business assumptions.
Model the financial implications of potential acquisitions, dispositions, developments and other strategic initiatives in partnership with Investments and other business functions.
Evaluate alternative financial scenarios and provide recommendations to support strategic planning and capital allocation decisions.
Provide financial analysis and recommendations to the Chief Financial Officer and senior leadership to support business and strategic decisions.
Assess the impact of business plans and strategic initiatives on liquidity, leverage, FFO, AFFO and other key financial measures.

Capital Planning
Coordinate Allied’s annual and long-term capital planning processes.
Consolidate forecasts for property capital expenditures, leasing capital, tenant improvements and development expenditures.
Monitor capital spending against approved plans and identify material variances, risks and emerging requirements.
Integrate capital plans into corporate forecasts and long-term financial models.
Provide analysis of the impact of capital investments on financial performance, liquidity and key REIT metrics.

FP&A Systems, Data and Continuous Improvement
Lead the development and enhancement of financial planning, forecasting and management reporting tools and processes.
Identify opportunities to automate and streamline financial planning and reporting activities.
Establish consistent financial models, reporting methodologies and performance measures across the organization.
Promote effective use of financial and operational data to improve business insight and decision-making.
Partner with Corporate Accounting and technology teams to support the effective integration of financial systems, data and reporting tools.
Champion continuous improvement and best practices across the FP&A function.

Leadership and Team Development
Lead, mentor and develop the FP&A team, fostering strong analytical, financial and business-partnering capabilities.
Establish clear priorities and expectations and promote a high standard of quality, accountability and collaboration.
Build strong relationships across Finance and the broader organization.
Develop organizational capability through coaching, knowledge sharing and succession planning.
Foster a culture of curiosity, continuous improvement and informed decision-making.

Qualifications

CPA designation required.
7+ years of progressive experience in accounting and finance within commercial real estate or property accounting.
Strong technical accounting and financial reporting experience, including full-cycle accounting processes.
Experience leading and developing high-performing teams.
Experience supporting budgeting and reforecasting processes in partnership with FP&A and operational teams.
Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across functions and levels of the organization.
Strong analytical, problem-solving and organizational skills, with a high level of attention to detail.
Experience with Yardi or similar property accounting systems is considered an asset.

Total Rewards and the Employee Experience

At Allied, total rewards are designed with the same perspective that shapes our operations. They are intended to support sustained contribution, creativity and a genuine sense of ownership in the work we do.

In practice, this includes:

Shared financial success and an ownership mindset

Eligible employees participate in performance-based bonus programs and a retirement savings program, with the option to invest in traditional funds or Allied units. This approach aligns individual effort with Allied’s long-term performance and reinforces a sense of ownership at every level of the organization.

Intentional presence and time off

In addition to vacation, employees receive six personal days and half-days before statutory holidays. Allied supports flexibility while maintaining a strong, in-person culture. This reflects how we collaborate most effectively and how we operate as a business.

Health, wellbeing and support

Comprehensive, company-paid health benefits include vision and dental coverage, along with a healthcare spending account. An employee assistance program is available to provide confidential support when it is needed.

Growth through leadership and exposure

Allied believes in leadership at every level. Employees are encouraged to contribute beyond the boundaries of their role, collaborate across disciplines and develop a broad understanding of the business. For those drawn to real estate, this includes uncommon exposure to how buildings, organizations and cities evolve through hands-on experience and shared responsibility.

Professional development grounded in practice

Learning at Allied is both formal and experiential. Ongoing professional development and a mentorship program support growth through structured learning and day-to-day engagement with experienced colleagues across the organization.

Purpose and connection beyond work

Each year, employees are provided with a paid volunteer day to contribute time and effort to a cause that is personally meaningful to them, reflecting our belief that contribution extends beyond the workplace.

If you are motivated by the role real estate plays in shaping cities and culture, and want your work to contribute to that effort, we encourage you to apply.

More insight into life at Allied, including our ESG and EDI initiatives, can be found in our annual ESG report.

Additional Information

We value human connection and experience. While Allied uses technology, including AI-enabled tools, to support administrative efficiency, all screening, assessment and hiring decisions are made by people.

We are committed to hiring the most qualified candidates with a dedication towards supporting diversity, equity and inclusion across our organization. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, ethnicity, origin, sexual orientation, disability and socioeconomic background. Diverse perspectives strengthen our organization and help us deliver better outcomes for our tenants, partners and communities. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

We strive to provide an accessible recruitment experience and welcome reasonable accommodation requests at any stage of the recruitment process. Please reach out to talent@alliedreit.com if support is needed.

We look forward to receiving your application.

new_jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
new_jobs.description:
About Allied

Allied is a leading owner-operator of distinctive urban workspace in Canada’s major cities. Our work is grounded in a clear purpose: to provide knowledge-based organizations with distinctive urban environments that support creativity, connectivity and human wellness.

Our vision is more expansive. We seek to make a continuous contribution to cities and culture that elevates and inspires the humanity in all of us. This vision informs how we operate, how we design and how we lead.

Real estate, for us, is not a passive investment. It is a profoundly human endeavour, one that must promote wellness, sustainability, diversity and creativity—today and for generations to come.

Allied is also a place to build a career of consequence. If you are looking for work that is thoughtful, tangible and enduring—work that contributes meaningfully to cities and the people who inhabit them—you will find purpose here.

For more information on Allied’s approach to city-building, visit our Insights page.

Purpose

Lead Allied’s financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis and management reporting activities.
As Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), you will lead budgeting and forecasting processes, develop long-term financial plans and provide analysis of financial and operating performance across Allied’s portfolio and corporate functions.

As a key member of the Finance leadership team, you will serve as a strategic business partner to senior leaders and help strengthen financial planning, analytical capabilities and financial discipline across the organization. This role is well suited to a collaborative and forward-looking finance leader with strong financial modelling and analytical capabilities and a commitment to developing people and building high-performing teams.

Responsibilities

Financial Planning, Budgeting and Forecasting
Lead budgeting and forecasting processes across the organization, establishing timelines, assumptions and requirements in partnership with key stakeholders.
Develop and own consolidated financial forecasts and multi-year financial plans.
Establish and track key performance indicators related to occupancy, leasing, operating performance, capital expenditures, financing and other business drivers.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to assess the financial implications of changing business and market conditions.
Continuously enhance planning and forecasting processes to improve accuracy, efficiency and business insight.

Performance Analysis and Management Reporting
Lead the preparation of monthly and quarterly management reporting for senior leadership.
Analyze actual financial performance relative to budget, forecast and prior periods, identifying key drivers of variances.
Analyze key performance indicators, including funds from operations (FFO), adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) and related financial and operating metrics.
Identify emerging trends, risks and opportunities and communicate their potential financial impact to senior leadership.
Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards and other reporting tools that provide clear visibility into organizational performance.
Lead the development of financial and performance reporting for the Board of Trustees and its committees.

Long-Term Financial Planning and Strategic Analysis
Lead the development and maintenance of Allied’s long-term financial model.
Assess the impact of changes in occupancy, leasing activity, rental rates, interest rates, capital expenditures, development activity and other key business assumptions.
Model the financial implications of potential acquisitions, dispositions, developments and other strategic initiatives in partnership with Investments and other business functions.
Evaluate alternative financial scenarios and provide recommendations to support strategic planning and capital allocation decisions.
Provide financial analysis and recommendations to the Chief Financial Officer and senior leadership to support business and strategic decisions.
Assess the impact of business plans and strategic initiatives on liquidity, leverage, FFO, AFFO and other key financial measures.

Capital Planning
Coordinate Allied’s annual and long-term capital planning processes.
Consolidate forecasts for property capital expenditures, leasing capital, tenant improvements and development expenditures.
Monitor capital spending against approved plans and identify material variances, risks and emerging requirements.
Integrate capital plans into corporate forecasts and long-term financial models.
Provide analysis of the impact of capital investments on financial performance, liquidity and key REIT metrics.

FP&A Systems, Data and Continuous Improvement
Lead the development and enhancement of financial planning, forecasting and management reporting tools and processes.
Identify opportunities to automate and streamline financial planning and reporting activities.
Establish consistent financial models, reporting methodologies and performance measures across the organization.
Promote effective use of financial and operational data to improve business insight and decision-making.
Partner with Corporate Accounting and technology teams to support the effective integration of financial systems, data and reporting tools.
Champion continuous improvement and best practices across the FP&A function.

Leadership and Team Development
Lead, mentor and develop the FP&A team, fostering strong analytical, financial and business-partnering capabilities.
Establish clear priorities and expectations and promote a high standard of quality, accountability and collaboration.
Build strong relationships across Finance and the broader organization.
Develop organizational capability through coaching, knowledge sharing and succession planning.
Foster a culture of curiosity, continuous improvement and informed decision-making.

Qualifications

CPA designation required.
7+ years of progressive experience in accounting and finance within commercial real estate or property accounting.
Strong technical accounting and financial reporting experience, including full-cycle accounting processes.
Experience leading and developing high-performing teams.
Experience supporting budgeting and reforecasting processes in partnership with FP&A and operational teams.
Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across functions and levels of the organization.
Strong analytical, problem-solving and organizational skills, with a high level of attention to detail.
Experience with Yardi or similar property accounting systems is considered an asset.

Total Rewards and the Employee Experience

At Allied, total rewards are designed with the same perspective that shapes our operations. They are intended to support sustained contribution, creativity and a genuine sense of ownership in the work we do.

In practice, this includes:

Shared financial success and an ownership mindset

Eligible employees participate in performance-based bonus programs and a retirement savings program, with the option to invest in traditional funds or Allied units. This approach aligns individual effort with Allied’s long-term performance and reinforces a sense of ownership at every level of the organization.

Intentional presence and time off

In addition to vacation, employees receive six personal days and half-days before statutory holidays. Allied supports flexibility while maintaining a strong, in-person culture. This reflects how we collaborate most effectively and how we operate as a business.

Health, wellbeing and support

Comprehensive, company-paid health benefits include vision and dental coverage, along with a healthcare spending account. An employee assistance program is available to provide confidential support when it is needed.

Growth through leadership and exposure

Allied believes in leadership at every level. Employees are encouraged to contribute beyond the boundaries of their role, collaborate across disciplines and develop a broad understanding of the business. For those drawn to real estate, this includes uncommon exposure to how buildings, organizations and cities evolve through hands-on experience and shared responsibility.

Professional development grounded in practice

Learning at Allied is both formal and experiential. Ongoing professional development and a mentorship program support growth through structured learning and day-to-day engagement with experienced colleagues across the organization.

Purpose and connection beyond work

Each year, employees are provided with a paid volunteer day to contribute time and effort to a cause that is personally meaningful to them, reflecting our belief that contribution extends beyond the workplace.

If you are motivated by the role real estate plays in shaping cities and culture, and want your work to contribute to that effort, we encourage you to apply.

More insight into life at Allied, including our ESG and EDI initiatives, can be found in our annual ESG report.

Additional Information

We value human connection and experience. While Allied uses technology, including AI-enabled tools, to support administrative efficiency, all screening, assessment and hiring decisions are made by people.

We are committed to hiring the most qualified candidates with a dedication towards supporting diversity, equity and inclusion across our organization. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, ethnicity, origin, sexual orientation, disability and socioeconomic background. Diverse perspectives strengthen our organization and help us deliver better outcomes for our tenants, partners and communities. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

We strive to provide an accessible recruitment experience and welcome reasonable accommodation requests at any stage of the recruitment process. Please reach out to talent@alliedreit.com if support is needed.

We look forward to receiving your application.
